run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-18T00:33:27Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is backed by real error spans: frontend-proxy 'ingress' spans return HTTP 504 after ~15.00 s, and their rate rose from a 0.011-0.026/s background to 0.13-0.32/s between 00:34 and 00:45. The sampled trace shows the whole chain: load-generator POST 504 -> frontend-proxy ingress 504 (15.001 s) -> frontend POST /api/checkout (15.719 s, HTTP 200) -> checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (15.716 s) -> checkout 'orders publish' producer span 15.582 s, while every other downstream call in that trace (cart, product-catalog, currency, shipping, quote, payment, email) stayed under ~85 ms. Checkout logs confirm the Kafka produce itself is the stalled step: before 00:30 writes took 127-286 microseconds, after the Kafka Deployment rollout restart at 00:30:56 the same writes take 11.4-23.0 s, and the share of checkout PlaceOrder spans over 10 s went from 0 to 0.93-0.99. The Kafka Deployment was restarted with an unchanged pod template (new ReplicaSet kafka-5c9d7cc485 carries only kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-18T00:30:56Z), and the 'orders' topic had to be recreated at 00:32:37. The only fault-injection setting found switched on in the cluster is in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config: kafkaQueueProblems defaultVariant 'on' (on=100), described as 'Overloads Kafka queue while simultaneously introducing a consumer side delay leading to a lag spike'; every other flag in that document is 'off', and only the flagd Deployment mounts that ConfigMap. Hypothesis: that setting is the root cause, the Kafka restart is its mechanism/timing, and the delayed produce path is what pushes frontend's /api/checkout past frontend-proxy's ~15 s response window into 504s. The conclusion is partial because the flag evaluation itself was not observed and the moment the flag was switched on (and what triggered the kafka rollout) cannot be established: change_history is not integrated.

claims.text: frontend-proxy 'ingress' error spans rose sharply: 5m error-span rate was 0.011-0.026/s from 00:20 to 00:33 (e.g. 0.0185 at 00:33), then 0.080 at 00:34, 0.133 at 00:35, 0.204 at 00:36, 0.296 at 00:39, and 0.243-0.321/s through 00:45, while total ingress spans stayed ~8.4-10.5/s.

The frontend-proxy error spans are 'ingress' spans with status tags error=true, http.status_code "504", otel.status_code "ERROR" and duration ~15,000,000 us (e.g. 15,001,259 us), each paired with a 'router frontend egress' span of ~15,000,841 us carrying error="true" and http.status_code "0".

In trace d3066bd6d4294c09a9c14e1f7b11fd20 the 504 originates in the checkout-to-Kafka publish: load-generator POST 504 (15.002 s) -> frontend-proxy ingress 504 (15.001 s) -> frontend POST /api/checkout and 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' 15.719/15.718 s (http.status_code 200) -> checkout 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' 15.716 s -> checkout 'orders publish' (producer) 15.582 s; cart GetCart 0.6 ms, product-catalog GetProduct 0.12 ms, currency Convert 0.69-0.76 ms, shipping /get-quote 84 ms, quote 0.32 ms, payment charge 34.7 ms, email send 2.7 ms.

checkout's Kafka writes were sub-millisecond before the Kafka rollout and seconds after it: logs show 'Successful to write message. offset: 0, duration: 127.203µs ... 286.151µs' between 00:29:28 and 00:29:59, then durations of 15.2-23.0 s at 00:33:43-00:33:58 and 11.4-19.2 s at 00:38-00:40.

The share of checkout server spans for 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' longer than 10 s was 0 through 00:32, then 0.058 at 00:33, 0.229 at 00:34, 0.754 at 00:36, 0.929 at 00:37 and 0.97-0.99 from 00:39 through 00:45 (histogram bucket difference against le="+Inf").

The kafka Deployment was restarted at 00:30:56 with an unchanged pod template: new ReplicaSet kafka-5c9d7cc485 was created 2026-11-18T00:30:56Z carrying only the extra annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-18T00:30:56Z, and its container spec (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-kafka, identical env, resources limits cpu 400m/memory 900Mi, requests cpu 100m/memory 300Mi, same labels) matches the older ReplicaSet kafka-ff7884766.

Events in otel-demo record that rollout: ReplicaSet kafka-5c9d7cc485 SuccessfulCreate 'Created pod: kafka-5c9d7cc485-hrd97' at 00:30:56Z, pod kafka-ff7884766-pn5m2 Killing at 00:30:58Z, ReplicaSet kafka-ff7884766 SuccessfulDelete at 00:30:58Z, Deployment kafka ScalingReplicaSet 0->1 and 1->0.

After the restart the Kafka broker had to recreate the 'orders' topic partition from empty: 'Sent auto-creation request for Set(orders)', 'CreateTopics ... CreatableTopic(name='orders', numPartitions=1, replicationFactor=1 ...): SUCCESS' at 00:32:34Z, 'Created log for partition orders-0' and 'Log loaded for partition orders-0 with initial high watermark 0' at 00:32:37Z.

ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config (key demo.flagd.json) contains flag 'kafkaQueueProblems' with state ENABLED, defaultVariant "on", variants {"off": 0, "on": 100} and description 'Overloads Kafka queue while simultaneously introducing a consumer side delay leading to a lag spike'; the same document's other fault flags (adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure) all have defaultVariant "off".
Of the 21 Deployments in otel-demo, only the 'flagd' Deployment mounts the flagd-config ConfigMap; no other Deployment references a ConfigMap holding fault-injection settings.

Kafka broker CPU is not saturated while the produce latency is sustained: the old pod kafka-ff7884766-pn5m2 used 0.008-0.021 cores, the new pod kafka-5c9d7cc485-hrd97 briefly used 0.207 (00:32) and 0.348 (00:33) and 0.134 (00:34) cores, then 0.006-0.033 cores from 00:35 to 00:44, against a 400m CPU limit.

checkout's own 'orders publish' producer spans carried STATUS_CODE_ERROR only in the windows covering 00:29-00:37 (0.07/s at 00:34, 0.0557/s at 00:35, 0.0528/s at 00:36, 0.0519/s at 00:37, 0 afterwards), while its non-error publish rate stayed near the pre-incident level (~0.28-0.49/s vs 0.51-0.64/s before 00:33).

Error-span rate by service over 00:09-00:45 was 0 for frontend, cart, currency, product-catalog, email, shipping, quote, payment, accounting and fraud-detection; ad and recommendation show only background 0.0037/s; checkout shows only a brief 0.0557-0.0519/s at 00:35-00:37; frontend-proxy is the service with the large sustained error rate.

All otel-demo pods are Running and ready with 0 restarts except fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-zcxzm, which has 2 restarts; kafka-5c9d7cc485-hrd97 started 2026-11-18T00:30:56Z with 0 restarts and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-bh295 started 2026-11-17T23:57:53Z with 0 restarts.

fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-zcxzm's last container termination was OOMKilled with exitCode 137, finishedAt 2026-11-18T00:24:01Z, and the container has been running since 2026-11-18T00:24:15Z (restartCount 2); a kubelet BackOff event for that pod is recorded at 00:24:02Z.

Most likely cause: the fault-injection setting kafkaQueueProblems (defaultVariant 'on', value 100) in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config is switched on and is delaying/overloading the Kafka publish path that checkout blocks on, so checkout PlaceOrder takes ~15.7 s, frontend's /api/checkout exceeds frontend-proxy's ~15 s response window, and frontend-proxy ingress spans return 504, producing the RequestErrorRate alert. The Kafka Deployment restart at 00:30:56 (unchanged template, restartedAt annotation) is the mechanism/timing marker; the sustained 11-23 s produce latency with the broker at ~0.02 cores of a 400m limit argues against broker CPU exhaustion and against the cold restart alone explaining it. Not yet proven: no flag evaluation for kafkaQueueProblems was observed in the sampled spans or logs.

Remaining alternative candidate: the kafka Deployment rollout itself (fresh broker with an empty /tmp log dir) is the sole cause, since the onset of slow PlaceOrder (00:33-00:34) follows the 00:30:56 restart and the 'orders' topic only reappeared at 00:32:37. It is weakened but not eliminated by the observation that produce writes were still 11-23 s at 00:38-00:40 while broker CPU was ~0.02 cores and writes succeeded.

fraud-detection's crash/restart is not the cause of this alert: its OOMKill (exitCode 137, 00:24:01Z) and BackOff (00:24:02Z) precede the 504 onset (PlaceOrder >10 s share still 0 at 00:32, first non-zero 0.058 at 00:33) by about nine minutes, its current instance has been running since 00:24:15Z, and its own error-span rate stayed 0 throughout 00:09-00:45.

The affected path is a latency/timeout path, not an error-returning backend: in the sampled trace frontend's own POST /api/checkout and 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' spans returned http.status_code 200 after 15.7 s, frontend's error-span rate was 0 across 00:09-00:45, and product-catalog, cart, currency, shipping, quote, payment and email calls in the same trace completed in under ~85 ms.

Switch the kafkaQueueProblems flag in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config back to 'off' (or remove the fault) and confirm that checkout produce durations return to microsecond/millisecond range and that frontend-proxy 504 spans stop; audit who/what triggered the kafka Deployment rollout at 2026-11-18T00:30:56Z.

gaps: change_history is not integrated, so I cannot tell when kafkaQueueProblems was changed from off to on, nor who/what issued the kafka Deployment rollout (only the mechanism mark kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-18T00:30:56Z is visible).

The declared fault itself was not directly observed: no flagd ResolveBoolean span or log line for kafkaQueueProblems appears in the sampled traces/logs, so the internal delay mechanism is inferred from the flag description plus the observed produce latency.

list_prometheus_rules queried with rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned no rules (status no_data), so the alert's exact expression and the annotation's reported value 0.4 could not be checked against the rule; the measured frontend-proxy ingress error-span rate peaked at ~0.32/s.

A 1-minute-resolution query of frontend-proxy ingress spans by status_code returned all-zero values while the 5-minute query returned non-zero values for the same period; onset timing therefore comes from 5-minute windows and is approximate (first rise between 00:33 and 00:34).
The old Kafka pod kafka-ff7884766-pn5m2 and its logs are gone, so the broker's own state before 00:30:56 and the reason for its replacement beyond the restartedAt annotation are unknown.

Which demo service evaluates kafkaQueueProblems (checkout producer vs a consumer such as fraud-detection) is not shown by the available evidence; therefore the exact hop where the delay is injected remains unknown.
Querying ResourceQuota objects in otel-demo returned no objects, so quota pressure could not be assessed either way from that query.
next_steps: Check the flagd/feature-flag change history or GitOps/audit trail to establish when kafkaQueueProblems became 'on' and why the kafka Deployment was rolled at 00:30:56Z.
Recommend setting kafkaQueueProblems back to 'off' and re-measuring checkout 'orders publish' span durations and frontend-proxy ingress 504 rate to confirm the causal link.

If the delay persists after the flag is off, inspect Kafka broker request-queue/produce latency metrics and the checkout Kafka producer configuration (acks, timeouts, connection settings) plus the frontend-proxy route timeout value.
